title: ReSIDS command result
description: The agent's answer to a command, and the record kept in the command log (GET /commands). Note what this is NOT: it is not the commit record. A response can be lost; the authoritative record that a command took effect is the EVENT it produced, carrying decided_by and command_id. A monitor that treats a lost response as a failed command, and reissues, is safe only because command_id makes execution at most once -- which is why that key is mandatory rather than advisory.

command_id.description: Echo of the command's idempotency key.

cmd_seq.description: Monotonic, gap-free position in the command log, assigned to EVERY command the agent answered -- accepted or rejected. Rejected commands produce no event, so without this log a refused actuation attempt (a stale view, a bad epoch, a forced override that failed) would leave no trace at all. It is reconciled exactly like the event seq: poll GET /commands?since=<highest contiguous cmd_seq>.

outcome.description: applied: accepted, and it commits at the next round boundary (HTTP 202) -- not yet in effect when you read this. no_op: the requested state was already the current state, so nothing was done and nothing is wrong (HTTP 200). rejected: nothing was applied (4xx).

replayed.description: true when this is the stored outcome of a command_id already seen. The agent did not execute anything a second time.

effective_round.description: The round at which the change takes effect, for outcome=applied. Commands commit on a ROUND BOUNDARY, never mid-round: a mode change applied halfway through an aggregation would split the round between two protocols. A command accepted during round r therefore takes effect at r+1.

event_seq.description: The seq of the event that records the commit, once emitted. This is the field that closes the loop between the two surfaces: the monitor correlates its command with the event, and treats THAT as proof.

state.description: The agent's state as it stands in the answer: mode, round, active_nodes, isolated_nodes, switch_pending, authority_epoch, last_seq. On a 409 this is what the monitor's stale view should be reconciled against.

warnings.description: Accepted, but with a consequence the commander should know. Two are expected in practice: isolating a node does NOT stop its traffic (removing it from the federation leaves whatever it emits on the monitored network untouched, so containment remains a network action); and isolating the last holder of a specialist narrows what the pool can type, even though recall holds.

code.description: expectation_failed: the expect block does not match reality (409). evidence_not_met: the agent's own safety condition is unmet, e.g. a GL->FL return while membership is incomplete (412, overridable with force). membership_floor: the isolation would take the federation below min_nodes (412). too_soon: flap protection, a commanded switch within min_switch_interval of the last one (429) -- without it a compromised commander could starve diffusion by oscillating the mode.

warnings: node 11 remains able to emit traffic: IDS-level isolation does not block it

error.detail: set_mode{to: federated} refused: membership full for 0 of 3 required rounds (2 nodes still absent). Returning to FL re-accepts the hub; the agent does not do that on an unmet condition unless force is set.
